Legal Standards.name: California Fish & Game Code § 5937
Legal Standards.note: Creates a direct legal duty on dam owners/operators to release sufficient water to keep fish populations below the dam in 'good condition.'

Legal Standards.name: Federal Endangered Species Act (ESA) § 7
Legal Standards.note: If your scenario involves federal actions, the action must avoid jeopardy/adverse modification.

Legal Standards.name: California Endangered Species Act (CESA)
Legal Standards.note: CESA prohibits 'take' of listed species; if low flows cause mortality/harm, projects may need authorizations.

Legal Standards.name: Bay-Delta Water Quality Control Plan
Legal Standards.note: Establishes flow-dependent water quality objectives to protect beneficial uses.

Legal Standards.name: Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act
Legal Standards.note: Requires protection of beneficial uses through water quality control plans.

Legal Standards.name: Clean Water Act (CWA) § 401
Legal Standards.note: California can condition federal approvals via 401 certification, including operational measures.

Legal Standards.name: California Constitution Article X, § 2
Legal Standards.note: All water rights/uses are limited by 'reasonable and beneficial use.'

Legal Standards.name: Water Code § 275
Legal Standards.note: Gives SWRCB/DWR a mandate to prevent 'waste' or 'unreasonable use.'

Legal Standards.name: Public Trust Doctrine
Legal Standards.note: Requires the state to consider and protect public trust uses when allocating water diversions.

Legal Standards.name: Central Valley Project Improvement Act (CVPIA) § 3406(b)(2)
Legal Standards.note: Dedicates a portion of CVP yield for fish, wildlife, and habitat purposes.

Legal Standards.name: Water Code § 1707
Legal Standards.note: Provides a legal pathway to change a water right to keep water instream for fish and wildlife.

Tier 1.policy_name: Reasonable Use / California Constitution Article X § 2 + Water Code § 275
Tier 1.note: Tier 1 is most consistent with state policy to prevent 'unreasonable use' and support public welfare, including ecosystem values.
Tier 1 most likely to avoid avoidable impairment to trust resources (fish, ecological and recreational values).

Tier 1.policy_name: Porter-Cologne beneficial uses / Bay-Delta Plan 'protection of fish and wildlife'
Tier 1.note: Tier 1 conditions are most likely to achieve flow-dependent beneficial-use protection.

Tier 2.note: Often consistent if remaining alterations don't create serious ecological harm in dry years.
Partial functional regime may cause dry-year recruitment failure or migration barriers for listed species, becoming insufficient for 'not likely to jeopardize' standard.
May be fine in many years but could be challenged if low-flow years produce demonstrable 'not in good condition' outcomes below a dam.

Tier 3.relationship: Likely met (where constraints mirror enforceable requirements)
Tier 3.note: Tier 3 aligns with existing requirements if baseline constraints encode D-1641-type minima. D-1641 is an enforceable order implementing Bay-Delta objectives.
Existing baseline minima are not guaranteed to satisfy no-jeopardy/no-take across all hydrologic sequences; legal standard is independent of model baseline.
Minimum flow constraint can still be too low to keep fish in 'good condition,' depending on dam, reach, and species.
Baseline minimums can be found unreasonable if they cause substantial avoidable degradation.

Tier 4.note: Persistent low flows harming fish condition below a dam becomes a prime enforcement hook.
'No function' conditions that harm listed species/habitat elevate jeopardy/adverse modification risk.
Same logic at state level if listed species are harmed.
'No function' is difficult to reconcile with protecting fish/wildlife beneficial uses where flow is controlling.

Tier 4.policy_name: Public Trust + Reasonable Use / Water Code § 275
Tier 4.note: Persistent ecosystem collapse increases likelihood that diversions/operations are unreasonable and inadequately protective of trust resources.

Governing Agencies.name: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB)
Governing Agencies.note: Water rights permits/licenses; Bay-Delta Plan; D-1641; public trust + reasonable use integration; some 401 certifications.

Governing Agencies.name: Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCBs)
Governing Agencies.note: Basin Plans and water-quality permitting/enforcement under Porter-Cologne (often where flow is needed to meet temperature/salinity/habitat objectives).

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW)
Governing Agencies.note: CESA implementation and fisheries expertise; participates in instream flow dedications.

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Water Resources (DWR)
Governing Agencies.note: SWP operator; subject to D-1641 for Bay-Delta standards.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (USBR)
Governing Agencies.note: CVP operator; implements CVPIA and ESA requirements; subject to D-1641 where applicable.

Governing Agencies.name: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS)
Governing Agencies.note: ESA consultations that frequently dictate operational/flow requirements.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS)
Governing Agencies.note: ESA consultations that frequently dictate operational/flow requirements.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. EPA
Governing Agencies.note: Federal permitting that can trigger ESA §7 and CWA §401 conditioning.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE)
Governing Agencies.note: Federal permitting that can trigger ESA §7 and CWA §401 conditioning.

Governing Agencies.name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)
Governing Agencies.note: Federal permitting that can trigger ESA §7 and CWA §401 conditioning.
